title: John Lennon live: Apollo Theatre, New York City | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono performed at the Apollo Theatre in Harlem, New York City, USA, on 17 December 1971.

They played to an audience of 1,500 at a benefit show for the families of people killed during the Attica State prison riot, which lasted from 9-13 September 1971. Thirty-three inmates and ten correctional officers and employees died; all but one guard and three prisoners were killed by law enforcement officers on the final day. It was the highest number of fatalities in the history of US prison uprisings.

Lennon and Ono played three songs: ‘Attica State’, ‘Sisters, O Sisters’, and ‘Imagine’. Lennon was somewhat coy in his introduction to the final song: “Some of you might wonder what I’m doing here with no drummers and no, nothing like that, but as you might know I lost me old band or I left it. I’m putting an electric band together, it’s not ready yet and these things like this keep coming up so I have to just busk it. So I’m gonna sing a song you might know. Its called ‘Imagine’.”

Also performing was Aretha Franklin. The event was filmed on 16mm tape, but received little mainstream press attention.

The performances of ‘Attica State’ and ‘Imagine’ were first released on the John Lennon Anthology box set in November 1998. ‘Imagine’ was also included on the Acoustic album in 2004. The full three-song set was finally released in the Power To The People box set in October 2025.

Paul McCartney performed at the Apollo Theatre on 13 December 2010.
